draft.title: What biotechnology is
card: Biotechnology is the use of living things, or parts of living things, to make products or to carry out useful processes.
uses whole organisms, such as yeast in bread, or microbes in cheese and yoghurt. People used these methods long before DNA was understood.
changes the genes of an organism so that it makes a product it would not make naturally. Bacteria with a human gene can make medicines such as insulin.
In each case, the living thing does the work. The product is made by cells, or by parts of cells such as enzymes.
draft.remember: Biotechnology means using living things or their parts to make products, from bread to medicines.

a.q: Which of these is an example of biotechnology?
opts: Using yeast to make bread rise
Using a kiln to bake clay pots
Using a pump to move water to crops
Using a furnace to melt iron ore
a.why: Yeast is a living organism, and its cells make the gas that makes dough rise. The other options use machines or heat and no living thing makes the product.
a.clue: Look for the option where living cells do the work.

b.q: Priya says that biotechnology only began when scientists first moved genes between organisms. Why is she wrong?
opts: People used living things such as yeast long before that
Moving genes is not a type of biotechnology
Biotechnology only uses parts of cells, not whole organisms
Biotechnology only applies to making medicines
b.why: Biotechnology is any use of living things or their parts to make products. Bread, cheese and yoghurt made with microbes count, and people made them long before gene transfer. Gene transfer is a modern form of biotechnology, not the start of it.
b.clue: Think about what people did with yeast and microbes in the kitchen.

a.best: Using yeast to make bread rise

b.best: People used living things such as yeast long before that

problems.detail: Question a is too easy for Year 12 HSC. The three distractors (furnace, pump, kiln) involve no living thing at all, and the clue ('where living cells do the work') points straight to the answer. Better distractors would be processes that seem biological but are not biotechnology.

proposal.title: What biotechnology is
card: Biotechnology is the use of living things, or parts of living things, to make products or to carry out useful processes.
uses whole organisms, such as yeast in bread, or microbes in cheese and yoghurt. People used these methods long before DNA was understood.
changes the genes of an organism so that it makes a product it would not make naturally. Bacteria with a human gene can make medicines such as insulin.
In each case, cells or parts of cells, such as enzymes, do the work. Killing microbes, or just cutting up a plant or animal as raw material, is not biotechnology.
proposal.remember: If cells or their enzymes do the work, from bread to insulin, it is biotechnology.

a.q: Which of these is an example of biotechnology?
opts: Using bacterial enzymes in washing powder to remove stains
Heating milk to kill the bacteria that would spoil it
Sawing pine trees into timber to build houses
Drying grapes in the sun to turn them into sultanas
a.why: Enzymes are parts of cells, and here they do the work of breaking down stains, so this is biotechnology. Heating milk involves bacteria, but it kills them rather than using them, and no cells do any work in sawing timber or drying grapes.
a.clue: Ask whether a living thing, or part of one, carries out the process.
